readings.title: Offerings for the Temple
readings.subtitle: A Heart of Generosity
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 29:1] And King Dawiḏ said to all the assembly, “My son Shelomoh, whom alone <dn>Elohim</dn> has chosen, is young and tender. And the work is great, because the palace is not for man but for <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn>. [2] “And with all my power I have prepared for the House of <dn>my Elohim</dn>: the gold for the gold, and the silver for the silver, and the bronze for the bronze, the iron for the iron, and the wood for the wood, shoham stones, and settings, antimony stones and many-coloured stones, and every precious stone, and white marble in blocks. [3] “And also, because I have set my affection on the House of <dn>my Elohim</dn>, I have my own possession of gold and silver, which I have given for the House of <dn>my Elohim</dn>, beyond all that I have prepared for the set-apart House: [4] three thousand talents of gold, of the gold of Ophir, and seven thousand talents of refined silver, to overlay the walls of the houses; [5] the gold for the gold and the silver for the silver, and for all the work by the hands of craftsmen. Who then is volunteering to fill his hand today to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>?” [6] Then the leaders of the fathers’ houses, and the leaders of the tribes of Yisra’ĕl, and the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, with the officials over the king’s work, volunteered. [7] And they gave for the work of the House of <dn>Elohim</dn> five thousand talents and ten thousand darics of gold, and ten thousand talents of silver, and eighteen thousand talents of bronze, and one hundred thousand talents of iron. [8] And those with whom were found precious stones gave them to the treasury of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, into the hand of Yeḥi’ĕl the Gĕreshunite. [9] And the people rejoiced, for they had volunteered, because with a perfect heart they had volunteered to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And King Dawiḏ also rejoiced with great joy.

readings.title: David's Prayer of Praise
readings.subtitle: Acknowledging the Source of All Wealth
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 29:10] And Dawiḏ blessed <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> before all the assembly. And Dawiḏ said, “Blessed are <dn>You</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ĕl, <dn>our Father</dn>, forever and ever. [11] “<dn>Yours</dn>, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, is the greatness, the power and the comeliness, the pre-eminence and the excellency, because of all that is in the heavens and in the earth. <dn>Yours</dn> is the reign, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>You</dn> are exalted as head over all. [12] “And the riches and the esteem come from <dn>Your</dn> presence, and <dn>You</dn> rule over all. And in <dn>Your</dn> hand is power and might, and in <dn>Your</dn> hand it is to make great and to give strength to all. [13] “And now, <dn>our Elohim</dn>, we thank <dn>You</dn> and praise <dn>Your</dn> comely Name. [14] “But who am I, and who are my people, that we should be able to volunteer so pleasantly as this? For all comes from <dn>You</dn>, and we have given to <dn>You</dn> out of <dn>Your</dn> own hand. [15] “For we are sojourners before <dn>You</dn>, and settlers, as were all our fathers. Our days on earth are as a shadow, and there is no abiding. [16] “O <dn>YeHoVaH our Elohim</dn>, all this store that we have prepared to build <dn>You</dn> a house for <dn>Your</dn> set-apart Name is from <dn>Your</dn> hand, and all is <dn>Yours</dn>. [17] “And I know, <dn>my Elohim</dn>, that <dn>You</dn> try the heart and are pleased with uprightness. As for me, in the uprightness of my heart I have volunteered all these. And now with joy I have seen <dn>Your</dn> people, who are present here, to volunteer to <dn>You</dn>. [18] “O <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> of Aḇraham, Yitsḥaq, and Yisra’ĕl, our fathers, guard this forever in the intent of the thoughts of the heart of <dn>Your</dn> people, and prepare their heart toward <dn>You</dn>. [19] “And give my son Shelomoh a perfect heart to guard <dn>Your</dn> commands and <dn>Your</dn> witnesses and <dn>Your</dn> laws, to do all, and to build the palace for which I have prepared.” [20] Then Dawiḏ said to all the assembly, “Now bless <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH your Elohim</dn>.” And all the assembly blessed <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> of their fathers, and bowed their heads and did obeisance to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and to the king.

readings.title: Solomon Anointed King
readings.subtitle: The Second Proclamation
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 29:21] And they made slaughterings to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and offered burnt offerings to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> on the next day: a thousand bulls, a thousand rams, a thousand lambs, with their drink offerings, and slaughterings in abundance for all Yisra’ĕl. [22] So they ate and drank before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> with great joy on that day. And they made Shelomoh son of Dawiḏ king the second time, and anointed him before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to be ruler, and Tsaḏoq to be priest.

readings.title: The Decline of David
readings.subtitle: A King in His Final Days
readings.text: [1 Kings 1:1] And King Dawiḏ was old, advanced in years. And they covered him with covers, but he could not get warm. [2] So his servants said to him, “Let a young maiden, a maiden, be sought for my master the king. And let her stand before the king, and let her be a companion for him. And let her lie in your bosom, so that my master the king gets warm.” [3] So they sought for a lovely maiden throughout all the border of Yisra’ĕl, and found <dn>את</dn> Aḇishag the Shunammite, and brought <dn>את</dn> her to the king. [4] And the maiden was very lovely. And she became a companion for the king, and served him, but the king did not know her.

readings.title: The Ambition of Adonijah
readings.subtitle: A Rivalry for the Throne
readings.text: [1 Kings 1:5] And Aḏoniyahu son of Ḥaggith exalted himself, saying, “I am king.” And he prepared for himself chariots and horsemen, and fifty men to run before him. [6] And his father had never grieved him at any time by saying, “Why have you done so?” And he was also very good-looking, and his mother bore him after Aḇshalom. [7] And he conferred with Yo’aḇ son of Tseruyah and with Eḇyathar the priest, and they followed and helped Aḏoniyahu. [8] But Tsaḏoq the priest, and Benayahu son of Yehoyaḏa, and Nathan the prophet, and Shim‛i, and Rĕ‛i, and the mighty men who belonged to Dawiḏ, were not with Aḏoniyahu. [9] And Aḏoniyahu slaughtered sheep and cattle and fatlings by the stone of Zoḥeleth, which is by Ěn Rog̱ĕl, and he invited <dn>את</dn> all his brothers, the king’s sons, and all the men of Yehuḏah, the king’s servants. [10] But he did not invite <dn>את</dn> Nathan the prophet, or Benayahu, or <dn>את</dn> the mighty men, or <dn>את</dn> Shelomoh his brother. [11] Then Nathan spoke to Bathsheḇa the mother of Shelomoh, saying, “Have you not heard that Aḏoniyahu son of Ḥaggith has become king, and our master Dawiḏ does not know it? [12] “And now, come, please let me give you counsel, and save <dn>את</dn> your own life and <dn>את</dn> the life of your son Shelomoh. [13] “Go and enter in to King Dawiḏ, and you shall say to him, ‘Did you not, my master, O king, swear to your female servant, saying, “Shelomoh your son shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne”? Why then has Aḏoniyahu become king?’ [14] “See, while you are still talking there with the king, I shall come in after you and confirm <dn>את</dn> your words.” [15] So Bathsheḇa went into the room to the king. Now the king was very old, and Aḇishag the Shunammite was serving <dn>את</dn> the king. [16] And Bathsheḇa bowed and did obeisance to the king. And the king said, “What is it you want?” [17] And she said to him, “My master, you swore by <dn>YeHoVaH your Elohim</dn> to your female servant, ‘Shelomoh your son shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne.’ [18] “And now, see, Aḏoniyahu has become king, and now, my master the king, you do not know it. [19] “And he has slaughtered bulls and fatlings and sheep in abundance, and has invited all the sons of the king, and Eḇyathar the priest, and Yo’aḇ the commander of the army, but he did not invite your servant Shelomoh. [20] “And you, my master, O king, the eyes of all Yisra’ĕl are on you, to declare to them who sits on the throne of my master the king after him. [21] “And it shall be, when my master the king sleeps with his fathers, that I and my son Shelomoh shall be counted as sinners.” [22] And see, while she was still talking with the king, Nathan the prophet came in. [23] And they told the king, saying, “See, Nathan the prophet!” And when he came in before the king, he bowed before the king with his face to the ground. [24] And Nathan said, “My master, O king, have you said, ‘Aḏoniyahu shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne’? [25] “For he has gone down today, and has slaughtered bulls and fatlings and sheep in abundance, and has invited all the king’s sons, and the commanders of the army, and Eḇyathar the priest. And see, they are eating and drinking before him! And they say, ‘Let King Aḏoniyahu live!’ [26] “But me, even me your servant, and Tsaḏoq the priest, and Benayahu son of Yehoyaḏa, and your servant Shelomoh, he did not invite. [27] “If this has been done by my master the king, then you have not made it known to your servant who sits on the throne of my master the king after him.”

readings.title: David Confirms Solomon
readings.subtitle: The King's Decree
readings.text: [1 Kings 1:28] And King Dawiḏ answered and said, “Call Bathsheḇa to me.” And she came into the king’s presence and stood before the king. [29] And the king swore and said, “As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives, who has redeemed <dn>את</dn> my life out of all distress, [30] as I swore to you by <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ĕl, saying, ‘Shelomoh your son shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne in my place,’ so I do this day.” [31] And Bathsheḇa bowed with her face to the ground, and did obeisance to the king, and said, “Let my master King Dawiḏ live forever!” [32] And King Dawiḏ said, “Call Tsaḏoq the priest and Nathan the prophet and Benayahu son of Yehoyaḏa to me.” And they came before the king. [33] And the king said to them, “Take with you <dn>את</dn> the servants of your master, and you shall set <dn>את</dn> Shelomoh my son on my own mule, and take <dn>את</dn> him down to Giḥon. [34] “And let Tsaḏoq the priest and Nathan the prophet anoint <dn>את</dn> him there as king over Yisra’ĕl. And blow the ram’s horn, and say, ‘Let King Shelomoh live!’ [35] “And you shall come up after him, and he shall come and sit on my throne, and he shall reign in my place. For I have appointed <dn>את</dn> him to be ruler over Yisra’ĕl and Yehuḏah.” [36] And Benayahu son of Yehoyaḏa answered the king and said, “Amĕn! May <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> of my master the king say so. [37] “As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has been with my master the king, so let <dn>Him</dn> be with Shelomoh, and make <dn>את</dn> his throne greater than the throne of my master King Dawiḏ.” [38] Then Tsaḏoq the priest, and Nathan the prophet, and Benayahu son of Yehoyaḏa, and the Kerĕthites and the Pelĕthites went down and set <dn>את</dn> Shelomoh on King Dawiḏ’s mule, and took him to Giḥon. [39] And Tsaḏoq the priest took <dn>את</dn> a horn of oil from the Tent and anointed <dn>את</dn> Shelomoh. And they blew the ram’s horn, and all the people said, “Let King Shelomoh live!” [40] And all the people came up after him, and the people played the flutes and rejoiced with great joy, so that the earth was rent with their noise. [41] And Aḏoniyahu and all the guests who were with him heard it as they finished eating. And Yo’aḇ heard <dn>את</dn> the sound of the ram’s horn and said, “Why is the sound of the city in such an uproar?” [42] While he was still speaking, see, Yonathan, son of Eḇyathar the priest, came. And Aḏoniyahu said to him, “Come in, for you are a brave man, and you bring good news.” [43] But Yonathan answered and said to Aḏoniyahu, “No, our master King Dawiḏ has made Shelomoh king! [44] “And the king has sent with him <dn>את</dn> Tsaḏoq the priest, and <dn>את</dn> Nathan the prophet, and Benayahu son of Yehoyaḏa, and <dn>את</dn> the Kerĕthites and <dn>את</dn> the Pelĕthites. And they have set <dn>את</dn> him on the king’s mule. [45] “And Tsaḏoq the priest and Nathan the prophet have anointed <dn>את</dn> him king in Giḥon. And they have come up from there rejoicing, so that the city is in an uproar. That is the noise you heard. [46] “And also, Shelomoh sits on the throne of the reign. [47] “And also, the king’s servants have come to bless <dn>את</dn> our master King Dawiḏ, saying, ‘May <dn>your Elohim</dn> make <dn>את</dn> the name of Shelomoh better than your name, and may <dn>He</dn> make <dn>את</dn> his throne greater than your throne.’ And the king bowed himself on the bed. [48] “And also, the king said this, ‘Blessed be <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ĕl, who has given one to sit on my throne today, while my eyes are seeing it!’ ” [49] And all the guests who were with Aḏoniyahu were afraid, and rose up, and each one went his way. [50] And Aḏoniyahu was afraid because of Shelomoh, so he arose and went and took hold of the horns of the altar. [51] And it was told Shelomoh, saying, “See, Aḏoniyahu is afraid of King Shelomoh. For see, he has taken hold of the horns of the altar, saying, ‘Let King Shelomoh swear to me today that he does not kill <dn>את</dn> his servant with the sword.’ ” [52] And Shelomoh said, “If he is a brave man, not a hair of him shall fall to the earth; but if evil is found in him, he shall die.” [53] So King Shelomoh sent, and they brought <dn>את</dn> him down from the altar. And he came and bowed himself to King Shelomoh. And Shelomoh said to him, “Go to your house.”
